name: pulse_hemorrhage
description: Untreated hemorrhage in the real Pulse whole-body adult engine; emits vital signs every second.

patient_file.description: Any patient instead of state_file: a name in <install>/bin/patients or a path; stabilized once (about 13 s), then cached

circuit_modifiers.description: Circuit path or node name -> multiplier on the value Pulse initializes it with; the patient is stabilized with them (about 25 s the first time, then cached)

pulse.doc:
Time-stepped bridge to the real Pulse whole-body adult engine.

The engine is loaded from a stabilized Pulse state file and advanced by
``interval`` seconds on every update. ``state_file`` names a state Pulse
ships; setting ``patient_file`` instead (a name in ``<install>/bin/patients/``
or a path) starts from that patient, stabilized once and then cached (see
``viva_pulse.patients``). Setting both raises. ``circuit_modifiers`` stabilizes
that patient with Pulse's configuration Modifiers (see ``stabilized_state``).
Interventions arrive as setpoints on the input ports and are forwarded to
Pulse as patient actions only when their value changes.

Inputs
------
hemorrhage_severity : overwrite[float]
    Hemorrhage severity in [0, 1] at ``config.hemorrhage_compartment``;
    0 stops the bleed.
iv_rate_mL_per_min : overwrite[float]
    Infusion rate of ``config.iv_compound`` (e.g. Saline, Blood); 0 stops it.

Outputs
-------
Vital signs (see ``VITALS``) as ``overwrite[float]``: ``initial_state()``
seeds each store with the loaded state's reading and every update emits
Pulse's current reading, so the store always equals Pulse's own value.
``irreversible_state`` turns True once Pulse reports an irreversible
state; the engine is not advanced after that, so the vitals stores keep
the last reading Pulse produced.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
